title: Respiration
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Respiration Worksheets (Aerobic, Anaerobic, Fermentation)
standard_code: KS3 Biology: Cellular processes and respiration
standard_text: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration in living organisms, including the breakdown of organic molecules to enable all the other chemical processes necessary for life; a word summary for aerobic respiration; the process of anaerobic respiration in humans and micro-organisms, including fermentation, and a word summary for anaerobic respiration; the differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration in terms of the reactants, the products formed and the implications for the organism.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on respiration: aerobic and anaerobic word equations, mitochondria, lactic acid and oxygen debt, yeast and fermentation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Aerobic needs oxygen and releases more energy; anaerobic needs none.
body_html:
How to think about it

Respiration is a chemical reaction in every living cell that releases energy from glucose.

  • Aerobic: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (in the mitochondria; releases a lot of energy).
  • Anaerobic in muscles: glucose → lactic acid. In yeast: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide.
  • After hard exercise we keep breathing hard to repay the oxygen debt.
Example

Yeast without oxygen makes?

Fermentation

Answer: ethanol + carbon dioxide

Example

Which type releases more energy?

Glucose is fully broken down

Answer: aerobic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration is breathing.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Saying respiration makes energy (it releases it).

faq.q: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
faq.a: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. It happens in the mitochondria and releases energy for the cell.
Respiration without oxygen. In human muscles glucose becomes lactic acid; in yeast it becomes ethanol and carbon dioxide. It releases much less energy.
Yes. All living cells respire all the time, day and night. Plants photosynthesise only in the light.
